title: Do the three angles of every triangle add up the same?
description: A line is drawn through the top corner of any triangle parallel to the base. The alternate angles move the two base angles to the top, where all three angles fill a straight line. A paper fold shows the same. Keeko's doubt is that measuring one triangle is a proof.
teaching_notes: One idea: the line through the top corner parallel to the base proves the angle sum for every triangle, because it uses no measurement. Watch for students who think a protractor reading on one triangle proves it for all.

source: Consider a triangle ABC. To find the sum of its angles, we can use the same method of drawing a line parallel to the base: construct a line through A that is parallel to BC. We know that ∠B = ∠XAB, ∠C = ∠YAC. So, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = ∠A + ∠XAB + ∠YAC = 180° as together they form a straight angle. Thus we have proved that the sum of the three angles in any triangle is 180°. This rather surprising result is called the angle sum property of triangles. There is a convenient way of verifying the angle sum property by folding a triangular cut-out of a paper.
video_script.why: The child has found the third angle of a triangle with a parallel line and now asks why the same works for every triangle.
video_script.substitution: A triangle of any shape, with no numbers, so that the proof holds for every triangle.
video_script.anchor: a triangle ABC of any shape with a line XY through A parallel to BC
video_script.wrong_answer: measuring one triangle proves it for every triangle
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko measures the angles of one triangle with a protractor and takes the sum as a proof for all triangles, but a measurement is rough and covers only that one triangle.
video_script.payoff_line: The three angles of every triangle add up to one hundred and eighty degrees

final_answer.spoken: the three angles of every triangle add up to one hundred and eighty degrees

maths_rules: XY is parallel to BC, so ∠XAB = ∠B and ∠YAC = ∠C (alternate angles)
∠XAB, ∠A and ∠YAC together make the straight angle XAY: ∠XAB + ∠A + ∠YAC = 180°
so ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180° for every triangle: the angle sum property
paper fold: the three corners folded in to meet at one point on the base fill a straight line, which is 180°
video_script.design: One triangle of any shape stays on the board with a line through the top corner parallel to the base. The two base angles are carried to the top by arrows, and a paper-fold picture shows the three corners meeting on the base.
